name: North Macedonia
summary: A yellow sun with eight broadening rays on a red field. It replaced the Vergina Sun flag in 1995 after a dispute with Greece.
origin: After independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, the republic adopted a red flag with the Vergina Sun, a 16-rayed star from the tomb of Philip II of Macedon. Greece regarded it as a Hellenic symbol and imposed a trade embargo.

Under the 1995 Interim Accord, the country adopted a new design by Miroslav Grčev: a stylised sun with eight rays reaching the edges. The country was renamed North Macedonia in 2019 under the Prespa Agreement; the flag was unchanged.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The field; red and yellow were the colours of the People's Republic of Macedonia.

symbols.name: Sun with eight rays
symbols.description: A yellow disc with eight rays widening toward the edges of the flag.
symbols.meaning: The 'new sun of liberty', referenced in the national anthem 'Denes nad Makedonija'.

facts: The rays touch the edges of the flag, making it one of the boldest designs among national flags.
Kyrgyzstan's flag also shows a yellow sun on red.
The 2019 Prespa Agreement also restricted official use of the Vergina Sun in North Macedonia.
clues: A yellow sun with eight rays spreading to the edges of a red field.
It replaced a 16-rayed star flag after a dispute with a southern neighbour.
Its sun is the 'new sun of liberty' from its national anthem.
